summary.intent: Get a status picture of the callisto repo (local git state, PRs, plans, Entire history), then continue the next piece of work: landing the unpushed v1 implementation work (T01-T05/T11) as a clean commit stack.
summary.outcome: Produced a full status report, then committed the dirty tree as a 5-layer stack (model, manifests, graph, cli, docs/changesets) by explicit path, leaving out Entire/Claude/Gemini tool settings. Nothing was pushed, and the transcript doesn't show per-layer cargo check or the full just ci run.

repo: Branch work/v1-implementation-stack holds 4 unpushed local commits plus about 83 uncommitted files (about 7.6k lines) covering T02-T05; no PR exists and the last activity was Sep 28-29.
0.9.0 and 0.10.0 shipped on Sep 27-28; ROAD-TO-V1.md's baseline (8ef9aa5a4, 'awaiting merge') and Stage 1 are stale.
Local commit T01 (verify generated decisions and applied PR heads) may overlap with #170, which already fixed the same verify step on main. This was not checked at the time of the status report.
The Cargo.lock +368 lines (36 new packages) comes from the new jsonschema 0.53 dev-dependency in callisto-cli, used by the JSON-schema tests.
version.rs, release.rs, lib.rs, runner.rs, cascade.rs and the CLI e2e tests carry hunks from several of the 10 changesets, so a per-topic commit split needs hunk-level patch surgery.
V1-VERIFICATION.md records component-wise checks passing on Sep 28 (1,862 tests, Clippy, 93.45% coverage, 25 release-workflow cases), but aggregate `just ci` hit a sandbox lock in cargo-deny.
Stages 3-5 of ROAD-TO-V1 (D01 owner-contract checkpoint, T06-T09, T10 generated workflows, T12 onboarding integration) have not started.
workflow: Entire tooling edits (.entire/settings.json, .claude/settings.json, .gemini/settings.json) show up in the dirty tree and must be excluded from feature commits. .entire/settings.json flips push_sessions/push_checkpoints on in a public repo, conflicting with the user's note that session transcripts stay private.
Stage by explicit path rather than `git add -A` when the working tree mixes feature work with tooling config.
When a topic split is infeasible, a layered stack by crate that builds at each step, with docs and changesets on top, is a pragmatic alternative.
A dry-run merge against origin/main detects conflicts without touching the working tree.

friction: Dirty tree mixed 10 changesets' worth of hunks across shared files, so the intended per-topic commits weren't practical.
Aggregate `just ci` couldn't run green in one pass because of a sandbox lock in cargo-deny.
Entire reports Claude hooks out of date and a legacy shadow branch, adding tooling noise to the repo.
open_items: Rebase the stack onto current origin/main and resolve overlap between local T01 and #170.
Run cargo check per layer and full `just ci` on the tip, then push as a native `gh stack` only after user confirmation.
Refresh ROAD-TO-V1.md baseline and Stage 1 status.
Start Stages 3-5: D01 owner-contract checkpoint, T06-T09, T10 generated workflows, T12 onboarding integration.

Clean up the Sep 27 stash, 174 unpushed Entire checkpoints, stale origin branches (fix/native-resolution, fix/release-forge-lookup, fix/release-pr-verify-envelope, docs/spec-rewrite), and run `entire enable --force` and `entire doctor`.
The uncommitted Entire/Claude/Gemini settings edits remain in the working tree, and untracked V1-FINDINGS.md, V1-VERIFICATION.md and how-callisto-works.md still need a decision.
